title: Catégorie des types de mots [dont arbres plans] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Γ is a 'graphe circulaire', meaning a finite graph with a cyclic order on the darts at each vertex. In modern terms this is a ribbon (fat) graph, or combinatorial map. Typically Γ is embedded in an oriented compact surface X.

(1) Cellular case. Cut X along the realisation |Γ|. The result is a surface with a canonical boundary, and that boundary carries a natural structure of topological polygon(s): a finite set of distinct marked vertices on each boundary circle. The resulting combinatorial polygon depends only on Γ, up to isomorphism. This is the classical inverse of building a surface by gluing the sides of polygons in pairs. When Γ is 'fondamental' (one face, X minus Γ a disc) you get a single 2n-gon, as in the normal form of a surface word.

(2) General ribbon graph. Grothendieck observes that the same construction works for an arbitrary circulated graph. It produces a canonical 'contour' C, which need not be connected: it is the boundary of the thickened ribbon graph. One component arises for each face, that is, each cycle of the face permutation.

He sets up the standard data:
- A⃗ is the set of darts (oriented edges).
- σ_Γ is the fixed-point-free involution reversing orientation.
- ρ_Γ is the 'rotation around the vertices' given by the circulation.
- S ≅ A⃗/ρ_Γ, provided Γ has no isolated vertex.

(3) Construction of C (completed on the next page). A crossed-out draft identifies A⃗ with the edges of C. The next page fixes this as a bijection rd: A⃗ → A(C), sending a dart to its 'right edge'; this orients each edge of C. Hence:
- the darts of C are A⃗(C) ≅ A⃗ × {±1};
- σ0^C = (id) × τ, with τ the sign swap;
- σ1^C is defined from the vertex rotation ρ_s, so that ρ^C(rd a) = rd(ρ_s a) and ρ^C(rg a) = rg(ρ_s^{-1} a).

Thus C is itself presented as a map in Grothendieck's (σ0, σ1) cartographic-group formalism: a disjoint union of polygons whose cyclic structure is the face permutation of Γ.

Purpose within file 152 ('types de mots', plane trees). This dictionary links surfaces cut along graphs to polygons with side identifications, that is, words. It is the combinatorial basis for passing between maps/dessins and words or polygon gluings.
errors: Not an error of Grothendieck's: the transcription's final formula 'C ≃ A⃗/ρ_Γ' should read 'S ≃ A⃗/ρ_Γ' (the vertex set). The proviso 'if Γ has no isolated vertex' only makes sense for vertices.

Minor gap: an isolated vertex (or a component with no edges) produces a boundary circle with no marked vertices, so not a polygon. The remark excludes this, but the general statement about the contour C is not adjusted.
The ρ/σ conventions (left versus right edge, ρ_s versus ρ_s^{-1}) are hesitant and partly crossed out. The construction is correct up to these orientation conventions.

ideas.what: Cutting a surface along an embedded graph yields a polygon (or polygons) whose combinatorial type depends only on the ribbon graph
ideas.modern_name: Face decomposition of a cellularly embedded graph; polygon-gluing / surface-word normal form
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Dehn–Heegaard, Brahana; combinatorial maps: Edmonds 1960, Jacques 1968, Tutte, Cori 1975)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (maps / dessins and triangulations), not in this form

ideas.what: Darts with an involution σ and a vertex rotation ρ; vertices = A⃗/ρ
ideas.modern_name: Permutation (rotation-system) description of combinatorial maps; Grothendieck's cartographic group (σ0, σ1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Edmonds, Jacques, Tutte, Cori; Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) for the cartographic-group language
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on maps and the cartographic group

ideas.what: Canonical 'contour' C of an arbitrary ribbon graph (possibly disconnected), itself encoded as a map with darts A⃗ × {±1}, σ0^C = id × τ, σ1^C defined via the rotation
ideas.modern_name: Boundary of the ribbon-graph thickening; face cycles (orbits of ρσ); boundary map / 'contour' of a fat graph
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in ribbon-graph theory (Penner, Kontsevich, Strebel-differential literature)

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but standard combinatorics of maps: cutting a surface along a ribbon graph to get polygons, and a dart/rotation encoding of the boundary contour. It is interesting mainly as context for how Grothendieck links maps to words in file 152. Nothing here is beyond the classical literature.
transcription_corrections: Final displayed formula: read 'S ≃ A⃗/ρ_Γ' (S = set of vertices), not 'C ≃ A⃗/ρ_Γ'. The proviso '(si Γ n'a pas de sommet isolé)' confirms this.
'ne dépend que de Γ, i.e. comme ens. pris.' should probably read 'ne dépend que de Γ, à isom. près.'
The superscript insertion in the first line is uncertain; the line likely reads 'Si Γ n'est pas [le graphe] fondamental' (i.e. if X∖Γ is not a single disc).

Crossed-out passage in the middle: 'L'ens. A⃗ s'identifie aussi à l'ens. des arêtes (via identifications: [...]) d'un contour C, d'où [σ0] ... il reste à définir σ1'. Here 'arêtes' replaces a struck word above the line.
Top-right marks: the '1' is a local page number (the next page is numbered '2'). The archive page number '6' is at bottom left.
